1.why: verify-reset looks the token up in resetTokens where it is bound to a specific accountId, and issues a grant tied to the session sid.

2.why: Codes are 256-bit random, single-use (deleted on verification), and mapped to one accountId, so a code cannot be used for any other user.

3.why: There is no session-invalidation logic on password reset, so any other session already marked authenticated would continue to work.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with a TLS cert/key plus HSTS, but the TLS protocol version is not pinned or verifiable as the latest.

5.why: Passwords are Argon2id-hashed and TLS protects transit, but reset codes are stored in plaintext in the in-memory resetTokens map rather than encrypted.

6.why: No real email exists; the simulated delivery message is generic about account existence but contains the code itself and is displayed in the page logs.

7.why: Email is normalized and regex-validated, inputs are length-capped, and all user-derived display uses textContent under a nonce-based CSP.

8.why: The only recovery/redirect link is constructed from location.origin with an encoded token; no user-controlled or external redirects exist.

9.why: There are no actual email templates; simulated messages are fixed server strings and the UI renders user data only via textContent with a strict nonce CSP.

10.why: The recovery code and MFA code are deliberately written to the on-page Logs panel and returned in API responses, so tokens are in fact shown.

11.why: Passwords are Argon2id-hashed, but the MFA code "246810" is hardcoded in the source and reset codes sit in plaintext memory.

12.why: No usable default password exists (only a fixture hash whose plaintext is unknown), but the static hardcoded MFA code acts like a default credential.

13.why: Server-side rate limiting with temporary lockout is implemented for request-reset (3/15min), verify (5/5min), login (5/5min), and MFA (5/5min).

14.why: request-reset returns the identical generic message and a delivery code whether or not the email matches an account, preventing account enumeration.

15.why: Codes are 32-byte CSPRNG hex tied to a single accountId record, though verification relies on token possession rather than re-binding to the requesting session.
